title: Add canary cohort forker with timeboxed mirroring and CI simulation hook
author: Ari Chen
description:
Motivation: intermittent prompt-set regressions can be masked by long-tail temporal shifts in production traffic. This change introduces a canary cohort forker that creates timeboxed mirror cohorts (hour/day windows) from historical prompt distributions and replays them against candidate model/service changes in CI. The goal is to detect transient regressions (semantic drift, latency tails) that don't show up in static anchor tests.

What this PR contains (single-line description body for CI ingestion): Adds a canary cohort forker, a lightweight timeboxed mirroring scheduler, an in-CI replay simulator, and a deterministic comparator exposing divergence/loss/latency signals; wires a new CI hook (ci/hooks/canary_mirror_hook) that runs in parallel with smoke/eval suites and emits a summarized gate decision.

Design and scope notes: the forker samples prompt sets using a jittered time-bucket approach to preserve production order statistics; we mirror both requests and metadata (client_id, route tags) to capture routing-dependent model behavior. The simulator runs a bounded replay (configurable token cap) to avoid CI budget blowouts and returns three primary metrics: semantic_divergence (CosSim/EM-like), responsive_latency_p95, and output_length_shift. The gate applies a configurable soft-fail policy (records failure and optionally blocks merges after N occurrences) and supports staged rollback budgets so ops can opt into automatic deprivation of canary traffic.

Checklist: 1) unit tests for sampler and comparator included; 2) integration smoke that runs a small replay on PRs under the canary label; 3) docs and runbook for interpreting gate signals; 4) lightweight telemetry for debugging (trace id propagation).

Related work: builds on ENG-3122 (anchor snapshotting) and ENG-3188 (regression replay infra). Linear tickets: ENG-3245, ENG-3301. No customer-facing API changes.

How to validate locally: run tools/cohort_simulator/run.sh --sample-window 1h --limit 500 then post results.json to ci/hooks/canary_mirror_hook local endpoint.

Rollout plan: enable in CI on a boolean flag; run as opt-in for 2 weeks for low-traffic repos, then flip to default for all eval-harness PRs if steady.

Notes on cost: replay cap defaults to 500 requests / PR; increasing this requires review.

Security: does not transmit PII - all prompt content is hashed in mirror by default; cleartext mirroring is opt-in and gated to internal runners.

review_comments: Sofia Martinez: Can the sampler preserve request ordering across buckets? If ordering is important we should document the guarantee. (response: we preserve intra-bucket order via deterministic seeding)
Liam O'Connor: Integration tests flaky on macOS runners — observed time skew failures. (response: switched to monotonic timers and added retry/backoff in runner)
Priya Desai: Is the semantic_divergence comparator stable across tokenizer changes? Suggest pinning tokenization config. (response: comparator now records tokenizer hash and fails closed if mismatch)
release_notes: Adds a canary cohort mirroring CI hook which replays timeboxed prompt cohorts to detect transient regressions. Configurable soft-fail gating and rollout options included. See docs/canary-cohort-runbook.md for operator guidance.
